title: Charlie DeBurgis and other musicians from her father's era
summary: She recalls bassist Charlie DeBurgis playing with her father around the country; Allen mentions Manetta's early years and his published piece Algiers Girl.

story.theme_name: Drummers and drumming: who played what, and how
story.community_name: Bass players: lineage, tone and technique

blocks.x: Do you remember if you ever played in Henry Allen's band? There's a young Henry Allen they call Red Allen now, but the old man that was also named Henry Allen... I think so.
...had a brass band that pushed famous over there. Because he played at all those bands. All of the different bands. Yeah. All those bands in that time. All those brass bands.
Do you remember any particular dance band groups that he might have worked with?
Well, I can only remember... One, he was a bass player. He was Charlie DeBurgis.
Oh, yes. Professor Mineta studied, took lessons from him. He did? He must have taught and played different instruments. He most had it.
When he was a boy... I do remember hearing my daddy play, say that Charlie DeBurgis played with them.
And played bass.
Yeah. They went all over little country places and played as far as Baton Rouge and all over, you know. Professor Mineta told us... He played dance music. Well, that was called the string dance.
He said he came down here from Arkansas or someplace up that way and was first playing guitar. He even played harmonica and different instruments of that kind.
He was a very good musician. Very good.

And I came across a piece that he wrote, I didn't get the entire piece, I think just the first page in the cover, called Algiers Girl. Just last year I found it. Mm-hmm. In the volunteers. And a lot of old sheet music I was going through. Professor Mineta had never seen it either.
He didn't know it was published. He hadn't seen it either. Well, I declare it.
So he had some music published at least then. And that was... Mr. DeBurgis then played with your father.
Yes, he did.
If you want to stop and answer the phone anytime, it's all right.
Is your dad in the bag?
So... Can you think of any other bands or musicians you might have worked with?
Well, that was about covered, playing with all the brass bands around here.
Yes, I put it. I meant in the dance band field or anything.
Well, I can only remember Charlie DeBurgis. You see, that was a little before my time. I mean, I was too young to even have an interest in it, you see.
